info.title: Forms
info.description: System register for forms and journeys. A form is a manifest-v2 form-page config with where its answers land; a journey is an ordered sequence of form, review and confirmation steps that may branch, write objects at declared steps and be saved part-way as draft objects.

x-openregister.description: Foundational forms register shipped by OpenRegister; backs the form and journey objects the run API drives.

forms.title: Forms
forms.description: Forms and the journeys that string them together.

form.title: Form
form.summary: A form as its own object: its page config, its audience and where its answers are written.
form.description: The config is a manifest-v2 `type: form` page config, validated by the same manifest validator an app manifest is, so a form body and a manifest form page cannot drift. Its writes, or its destination and mapping, name where a submit lands; the mapping is judged against the destination schema when the form is saved.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the form is for, for the people who maintain it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Only a published form or journey can be filled in or started.

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: Who may fill it in: anyone (public), a signed-in user (authenticated) or staff only (internal).

config.title: Form config
config.description: A manifest-v2 form-page config (`config.fields[]`, `config.steps[]`, per-field validation and visibleWhen).

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: The one register and schema a submit writes into, when the form writes one object.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: How form fields map onto the destination schema: `fields[]` of { field, property } and `fixed` values.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: The objects a submit writes, in order: { register, schema, mapping, as }. A fixed value { "$write": "<as>" } is the id of an earlier write.

journey.title: Journey
journey.summary: An ordered sequence of form, review and confirmation steps, with branching, writes and access.
journey.description: A journey is UI-facing: it may trigger a flow, and it is not one. Each step is { id, type, form?, fields?, next?, writes? }; a next rule is { when, step } where `when` is the manifest `visibleWhen` condition. Objects are created or leave draft only at a step declaring writes, all or none. Access is required and never inferred.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the journey is for, for the people who maintain it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Only a published form or journey can be filled in or started.

access.title: Access
access.description: Who may start it: anyone without a session (anonymous), a signed-in user (authenticated) or a user with a verified trust level (minTrust).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: create starts new objects; update changes one existing object opened through an access link.

form.description: The form object whose config this step renders.

fields.description: The fields this step asks for.

next.description: Branching rules { when, step }; the first whose condition holds names the next step.

writes.description: The objects this step writes when answered: { register, schema, mapping, as }.
